name: Living Goods' community health workers (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The locations the sheet's bottom line reads (row labels naming Kenya, Uganda, Burkina Faso), sharing equally.

missing_data.note: Partly thin (50%): Living Goods counts its health workers' treatments, pregnancy registrations and contraception, but the deaths averted are The Life You Can Save's projection from case-fatality rates and studies of community treatment, credited by growth since an earlier year rather than against a comparison group.

summary: Living Goods supports community health workers in Kenya, Uganda and Burkina Faso who treat sick children at home for malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea and follow pregnant women. The Life You Can Save credits Living Goods with the rise in treatments and pregnancy registrations since an earlier year, estimates the children's and mothers' deaths averted from case-fatality rates and studies of community treatment, and divides by the learning sites' costs. Our view values the deaths the site's way, adds the family planning the health workers provide, and counts the whole programme's spending from Living Goods' accounts; the biggest uncertainties are the deaths averted per treatment and how much of the care would have happened anyway.

sections.title: The Life You Can Save's figures pooled
Deaths valued the site's way, and family planning
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: children's and mothers' deaths averted are valued like every death on the site; the family planning the health workers provide, which the sheet leaves out, is valued with the site's shared figure.

sections.title: The whole programme's cost
sections.explainer: charityevals' step. The sheet's costs are only the learning sites' devices and supplies (1.3 million dollars), against the treatments of all of Living Goods' health workers in the three countries: the 1,540,361 children treated in 2024 are exactly the number its Form 990 for 2024 reports for the whole programme, which cost 21.3 million dollars. Our view counts the programme's spending behind the added treatments.

story.sentence: $1,000 pays community health workers to treat sick children at home. Every **{(cost_burkina_faso + cost_kenya + cost_uganda) * cost_multiplier / (child_deaths_total * counterfactual_share)|$}** saves **a young child's life**.

rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The sheet counts a mother's death as her remaining life expectancy, discounted (24 to 24.6 years); the site uses GiveWell's weight for a death at 15 to 49 times the value-of-a-life slider.

rows.label: Share of the added treatments' effect that wouldn't have happened without Living Goods
rows.explainer: Our judgment, ×1 (60% to 100%): the sheet credits only the rise in treatments since the baseline year, and its mortality reductions are those of community treatment against care as usual. Some sick children would have reached a clinic or a government health worker anyway.

rows.label: Illness shortened and hospital stays avoided, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer: The sheet counts only deaths. Prompt treatment also shortens illness and spares hospital admissions (the sheet's notes cite 19% fewer severe malaria admissions). Our judgment, 5% (0 to 15%).
